entities.name: Kyoto Prefectural University of Medicine
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
Kyoto Prefectural University of Medicine (京都府立医科大学, Kyōto Furitsu Ika Daigaku), founded in 1872 as a medical school (one of Japan's earliest Western medicine institutions) and established as a full university in 1921 — is a prestigious specialized medical university in Kyoto, Japan, with a long history of medical education and research that places it among Japan's historically important medical institutions, having trained doctors for 150 years in the city that was Japan's imperial and cultural capital.

The 1872 founding of Kyoto's prefectural medical school was part of the Meiji government's urgent program to introduce Western medicine to Japan — replacing or supplementing traditional Chinese-influenced Kampo medicine with the European scientific medicine that the Meiji reformers believed was essential for national strength and modernization. Medical education was a high priority: Meiji Japan needed trained doctors to improve public health, treat industrial injuries, support military capacity, and demonstrate Japan's civilizational advancement to Western powers.

Kyoto Prefectural University of Medicine's 150-year history spans Japan's transformation from feudal to modern: training doctors during the Meiji industrial revolution, through the militarist period (wartime medical research), post-WWII reconstruction, and Japan's emergence as a leading global economy. The university's attached hospital is one of Kyoto's major medical centers. Research conducted at the university has contributed to Japanese medical science, and its graduates have practiced throughout Japan and internationally.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Kyoto Prefectural University of Medicine — one of Japan's earliest Western medicine institutions (1872), training doctors for 150 years during Japan's entire modern transformation — is historically significant as a monument to Meiji medical modernization and a century and a half of Japanese medical education.
